channel.title: The Grant Desk - Journalism & Writers, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Journalism & Writers, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: BFI NETWORK England: Early Development Fund (GBP 3,000-5,000 treatment awards for debut long-form writers) (closes 11 Nov)
item.description:
BFI NETWORK (BFI, National Lottery funding)
Deadline: 11 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 3,000 to 5,000 per project to develop a treatment (stage one). Projects completed to schedule can then apply for second-stage funding to write a full first draft. National Lottery funding; no application fee stated.

BFI NETWORK's Early Development Fund supports writers at the very start of a debut long-form project: those who do not yet have a first draft of a script (or the equivalent format for immersive work).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellowships 2027-28 (University of Michigan) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 85,000 stipend plus USD 5,000 relocation (figures from secondary listings; confirm on the official site).

An academic-year fellowship for mid-career journalists to pursue a study project at the University of Michigan, with seminars and programming at Wallace House. DEADLINES: international applicants 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm ET; US applicants 1 February 2027. No application fee stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: National Geographic Society: The Human Thread RFP (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
National Geographic Society (Center for Human Histories and Cultures, with support from Lilly Endowment Inc.)
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Level I: up to US$20,000 (for applicants new to National Geographic funding, one year to implement). Level II: up to US$100,000 (for more established applicants, two years to implement).

Request for proposals from the National Geographic Society's Center for Human Histories and Cultures, funded by Lilly Endowment Inc.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: European Press Prize 2027 (journalism awards, EUR 10,000 per category, Council of Europe countries) (closes 10 Dec)
item.description:
European Press Prize
Deadline: 10 Dec 2026
Award: EUR 10,000 per category winner in the 2026 edition (five categories); 2027 amounts not yet confirmed. No entry fee found.

Europe's main journalism award, recognising outstanding reporting published in the previous year. Entries opened 1 November 2026. CATEGORIES (2026 edition; 2027 list not yet confirmed): Distinguished Reporting, Investigative Reporting, Innovation, Migration Journalism and Public Discourse.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cove Park Awarded Residencies 2027-2028 (Scotland, UK, Central and South America and diasporas) (closes 11 Dec)
item.description:
Cove Park
Deadline: 11 Dec 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: Fully funded: GBP 775 per week fee (VAT inclusive, freelance), travel allowance (Scotland GBP 65 to 200, rest of UK up to GBP 250, Europe up to GBP 400, other international up to GBP 1,250), materials up to GBP 150 for studio-based practitioners, private accommodation and studio, visa and access support. Application Access Bursary available (request by 30 November 2026). No application fee.

Cove Park's biennial call for fully funded Awarded Residencies at its 50-acre rural residency site in Argyll, on the west coast of Scotland, programmed between May 2027 and December 2028.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: HKADC Cultural Exchange Project Grant (up to HKD 500,000 for Hong Kong artists working abroad) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
Hong Kong Arts Development Council (HKADC)
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026, 18:00 Hong Kong time
Award: General Version: up to HKD 500,000 for individual artists and arts organisations, covering all project expenditure except listed exclusions; up to HKD 800,000 for experienced organisations with large-scale, outstanding exchange projects. Trial Version: up to HKD 150,000 for transportation, freight, insurance and documentation only. No application fee stated.

The Hong Kong Arts Development Council's Cultural Exchange Project Grant supports Hong Kong artists and arts organisations taking work abroad: overseas exhibitions, performances, festival participation, residencies, touring and similar exchange activity, across music, dance, xiqu, drama, visual...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: HKADC Emerging Artists Development Grant (up to HKD 90,000, Hong Kong arts graduates) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
Hong Kong Arts Development Council (HKADC)
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026, 18:00 Hong Kong time
Award: Grant ceiling HKD 90,000 per project (HKADC may exceed the ceiling for projects of great potential, subject to resources). No application fee stated.

The Hong Kong Arts Development Council's Emerging Artists Development Grant funds a first arts project by recent graduates: performances, exhibitions, publications, creation of artwork, translation and other project types allowed under its general Project Grant.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: In Development x Asterisk Essay Contest: How Will AI Affect Developing Countries? (USD 10,000 top prize) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
In Development and Asterisk Magazine, with a special prize from the African Tech Futures Lab
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026
Award: Winner USD 10,000 plus publication in Asterisk (print and online) and In Development; two runners-up USD 5,000 each plus publication in Asterisk (online) and In Development; two honourable mentions USD 2,000 each. Separate African Tech Futures Lab prize of USD 2,500 for the best essay by an African national, combinable with the main prizes. No entry fee stated.

An essay contest run by the development-economics publication In Development and Asterisk Magazine on how transformative AI will affect low- and middle-income countries, and how those countries might respond.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Royal Institute of Philosophy Essay Prize 2026: Humans and AI (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
Royal Institute of Philosophy
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 1,000 cash plus GBP 500 of Cambridge University Press books; the winning essay is published in the journal Philosophy.

The Royal Institute of Philosophy's annual essay prize asks for an original philosophical essay on the 2026 topic, Humans and AI. Essays of up to 8,000 words, anonymised for review, are submitted by email. No eligibility restrictions are stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: The Stringer Awards 2027 (independent accountability journalism) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
Stringer Journalism Foundation
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026
Award: USD 9,000 to 100,000 per award, multi-year and unrestricted; the size depends on funds raised.

The Stringer Awards give unrestricted, multi-year funding to independent journalists who expose abuses of power, in Senior and Emerging categories. No nationality restriction is stated. No application fee.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship 2027-28 (MIT) (closes 9 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
Deadline: 9 Jan 2027
Award: USD 87,500 stipend over 9.5 months, plus USD 5,000 for travel and housing, health insurance and a childcare subsidy. No application fee.

An academic-year fellowship at MIT for journalists covering science, health, technology or the environment, with seminars, MIT and Harvard courses and a self-directed study project.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Journalismuspreis Informatik 2026 (German-language journalism on computing and society) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Saarland Ministry for Digital Affairs with Saarland Informatics Campus
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 CET
Award: EUR 5,000 in each of three categories (Text, Audio, Video/Multimedia).

An award for German-language journalism that explains computer science and its impact on society, for work published in 2026. Three categories (Text, Audio, Video/Multimedia) each carry EUR 5,000. Submissions open 2 November 2026 and close 15 January 2027, 23:59 German time.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IJ4EU Freelancer Support Scheme 2026-27, Second Call (cross-border teams of freelance journalists) (closes 2 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU): International Press Institute and European Journalism Centre
Deadline: 2 Feb 2027
Award: Up to EUR 20,000 per team, plus training and mentoring.

A strand of IJ4EU for freelance journalists: teams of at least two freelancers in two eligible countries receive funding, training and mentoring for a cross-border investigation.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IJ4EU Investigation Support Scheme 2026-27, Second Call (cross-border investigative journalism) (closes 2 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU): International Press Institute and European Journalism Centre
Deadline: 2 Feb 2027
Award: EUR 5,000 to 50,000 per project, from a EUR 1.2 million pot.

IJ4EU funds cross-border investigative journalism in the public interest, by teams of journalists and newsrooms working across at least two eligible countries. Eligibility is by country of residence, not citizenship; applications are in English.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Outrider AI + Nuclear Reporting Fund (rolling)
item.description:
Outrider Foundation
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Up to USD 10,000 per reporting project.

Outrider funds journalists and outlets reporting on the intersection of artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons: how AI is changing nuclear risk, command and control, and policy. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the Google Form linked from the fund page. No application fee.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Inciter Art (Fractured Atlas): quarterly open call for essays, 'tending to the hearth' (USD 750 stipend)
item.description: Fractured Atlas (Inciter Art) · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · USD 750 stipend per selected writer, paid by ACH deposit or check once the first draft is finished (a W-9 form is required). No submission fee.

item.title: The Open Notebook Early-Career Fellowship 2027 (remote)
item.description: The Open Notebook · deadline 31 Oct 2026 · USD 6,600 stipend over the twelve-month part-time fellowship, plus one-on-one mentoring from an experienced science journalist and published clips at The Open Notebook. No application fee.

item.title: J. Anthony Lukas Work-in-Progress Awards 2027
item.description: Columbia Journalism School and the Nieman Foundation · deadline 03 Dec 2026 · Two awards of USD 25,000 each. No entry fee for the Work-in-Progress awards.

item.title: La Scam: Bourses Brouillon d'un reve Sonore (Radio and Podcast Authors, rolling)
item.description: La Scam (Societe civile des auteurs multimedia) · deadline Rolling / undated · EUR 2,500 to EUR 6,000 per bourse, paid directly to the author 4 to 5 weeks after contract signing; over EUR 830,000 is distributed annually across all Brouillon d'un reve categories. No application fee.

item.title: Stiftung Kunstfonds: KUNSTFONDS_Publikation 2027 (up to EUR 24,000)
item.description: Stiftung Kunstfonds · deadline 15 Jan 2027 · Up to EUR 24,000 per publication project; a minimum 10% own contribution is required and may come from third parties. No application fee.
